questions.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ and $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=-3{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2},\,$ $T({b}_{2})={c}_{1}-4{c}_{2}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{3})=5{c}_{1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=-3{c}_{1}-5{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})={c}_{1}-4{c}_{2} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3})=5{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2})$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 5 \\ -5 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=-4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ -2 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
